holes_found.description: The new Boulder quiet-day comparison is reported as point values with no noise floor, and its sign at the dome's 17:20 timestamp depends on the alignment choice. rev2 says Z was '+0.8 nT at the dome's 17:20 UTC and +4.9 nT at eclipse maximum' (detail_evidence) and the TLDR says 'the vertical component the dome uses was slightly higher than on quiet days, not 10.9 nT lower, so the dome's number comes from its choice of baseline' (tldr_evidence). Recomputed this run on the same 23 input files (sha256 all match monitor/analyst/analysis-records/win010-c17-rev2-verification-20260929.json:scripts[0].output.inputs_sha256). (a) I reproduce +0.75 / +4.91 exactly. (b) Leave-one-out null: treating each of the five quiet days as a pseudo-eclipse day against the mean of the other four, with the same pre-eclipse-hour alignment, gives Z at 17:20 of −1.2, −15.2, +9.6, +6.3, +0.5 nT (population sd 8.6 nT); with an IQD-style set (2, 9, 15, 26, 28 Aug) it is −11.3, −4.6, −0.8, +10.0, +6.7 (sd 7.7). A single-minute value at one station therefore carries roughly ±8 nT of day-to-day noise, and the dome's −10.9 sits only about 1.3–1.4 sd from our +0.8. (c) Changing only the alignment (pre-eclipse hour / night 06–09 UT / daily mean / none) moves the 17:20 value from +1.1 to −3.8 nT, so under two of four reasonable alignments Z at 17:20 is slightly LOWER than on quiet days. At eclipse maximum it is higher under all eight set-and-alignment variants (+0.3 to +4.9). A defender can say: 'your own quiet days disagree with each other by 15 nT at 17:20, and your sign flips with the alignment; you cannot exclude our −10.9 from Z alone.' This is the same overstated-precision pattern as EXP-687 C3-2 (fit uncertainty not calibrated on control days), now in a verdict-bearing panel and its TLDR.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace the point-value sentences with the robust statements: (1) across two quiet-day sets and four alignments, eclipse-day Z at 17:20 lies between −3.8 and +1.1 nT and at maximum between +0.3 and +4.9 nT, never near −10.9; (2) quiet days differ from each other by about ±8 nT at a single minute, so Boulder Z alone cannot confirm or exclude a ~10 nT effect; (3) the decisive evidence is the distribution test in hole 1; (4) Meza et al. (smoothed and detrended) find dZ about +3 nT, sign positive. Suggested tldr_evidence middle sentence: 'At Boulder in 2017 the eclipse shows mainly in the north-south component; the vertical component the dome uses shows no detectable dip, and the dome's −18.22 nT figure is what Boulder's Z does on an ordinary August afternoon.' Add the leave-one-out and alignment-sensitivity outputs to the analysis record (provenance_type computed).

holes_found.description: 'The same measure' is not the same measure, and the correctly matched test is much stronger. rev2 says 'The same measure on the five quiet days, with no eclipse, gives −9.3 to −27.3 nT' (detail_evidence) and the finding says the −18.22 nT figure 'is matched by ordinary quiet days at Boulder on the same measure (−9 to −27 nT)'. The dome's OPEN-009 measure is the eclipse-window minimum MINUS THE PREVIOUS DAY'S daily mean (05-model.txt:474, 'Aug 20 daily mean ... vs eclipse min'). The analysis script subtracts each quiet day's OWN daily mean (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/win010-c17-rev2-verification-20260929.json:scripts[0].source, same_stat block: st.mean(zd.values()) for day d). Recomputed on the dome's actual measure: the five quiet days give −26.2, −29.1, −7.7, −7.4, −7.7 nT (range −7.4 to −29.1, not −9.3 to −27.3). Across all 29 non-eclipse days of 2–31 August 2017 the median is −19.9 nT, 16 of 29 days reach −18.22 or lower, and the eclipse day's −18.22 sits at about the 45th percentile. A defender who re-runs the dome's formula gets numbers different from ours, which is a replication failure even though our conclusion survives.
holes_found.recommendation: Fix the finding and detail_evidence to: 'On the dome's own measure (lowest Z in the eclipse window minus the previous day's mean), the other 29 days of August 2017 give a median of −19.9 nT, and 16 of them reach −18.22 nT or lower; the eclipse day is ordinary.' If the five-quiet-day figures are kept, give them as −7.4 to −29.1 nT, or label the own-day variant as a different statistic. Add the prev-day-mean variant to the analysis record with its output.

holes_found.description: The dome's 'quiet-day' baseline, 20 August 2017, was a G1 storm day, and rev2 repeats the dome's label instead of testing it. GFZ definitive Kp (kp.gfz.de Kp_ap_Ap_SN_F107_since_1932.txt, fetched this run) for 2017-08-20: 4+, 5o, 3o, 2+, 2+, 3+, 3o, 3o (Kp 5o at 03–06 UT = NOAA G1; six of eight slots at 3o or above; Ap 20). For 2017-08-21: day maximum 3o, Ap 9. The dome wrote 'Aug 21 was geomagnetically disturbed pre-eclipse — Aug 20 quiet-day baseline is most defensible' (05-model.txt:474), so its 'quiet' reference was more disturbed than the day it rejected as disturbed. That is a dome-internal contradiction of exactly the kind rev2's 'Kp argument, corrected' paragraph is built on, and it is missing. Meanwhile rev2 adopts the label without quotation marks (detail_verdict_text: 're-audited the same 2017 event at −18.22 nT against a 2017-08-20 quiet-day baseline') and uses 20 August as a comparator (detail_evidence: 'On the dome's own chosen quiet day, 20 August, Z at 17:20 UTC was 6.0 nT lower than during the eclipse'). That 6.0 nT is a raw single-day difference with no alignment (it is +1.3 with the pre-eclipse-hour alignment), single days carry ±8 nT noise (hole 0), and 22 August on the same basis gives +15.7 nT. A defender can turn it round: 'you compare us against a storm day when it suits you.'
holes_found.recommendation: Put 'quiet-day' in quotation marks wherever the dome's label is reported, and add one sentence to 'The Kp argument, corrected': 'The dome's re-audit uses 20 August 2017 as its quiet-day baseline because 21 August was disturbed before the eclipse; on the GFZ record 20 August reached Kp 5o (G1 storm level) with Ap 20, against a peak of 3o and Ap 9 on the eclipse day.' Delete the 20-August 6.0 nT sentence.

holes_found.description: 'first proposed for eclipses by Chapman in 1933' (tldr_evidence; finding has the same phrase) is not supported, and this is the fourth wording problem in the Chapman cluster. Magnetic effects of eclipses were sought and reported decades earlier: Bauer (1900), 'Résumé of magnetic observations made chiefly by the United States Coast and Geodetic Survey on the day of the total solar eclipse, May 28, 1900', Terr. Magn. Atmos. Electr. 5(4):143, doi 10.1029/te005i004p00143, and Bauer's 1905 eclipse campaign (Science 22:411, doi 10.1126/science.22.561.411) (Crossref bibliographic, this run; contents not opened). What Chapman (1933) did first was work the effect out for an E-layer Sq current system. A reader who checks the history sees us correct one Chapman claim by inserting another unsourced one. Rated moderate rather than major (TLDR rule) because I verified only that earlier observational work exists, not whether it proposed a mechanism; the replacement wording below is safe either way and costs nothing.
holes_found.recommendation: tldr_evidence and finding: 'an effect Chapman worked out for the ionospheric current system in 1933 and that INTERMAGNET data confirmed statistically by 2018'. detail_evidence already says 'worked out what an eclipse should do to that current system' — keep that. Fold the same wording into the open Chapman cross-surface issue-proposal (proposal-chapman1933-5to25nT-cross-surface-1790717668315.json).

hnote_responses.i_bou_z_attack: Inputs reproduce (23/23 sha256 match). The dome's −18.22 nT reproduces exactly (min 19:07 UT, which is 12:06 local mean solar time at 105.24°W — the normal Sq Z minimum near local noon). Would a reasonable alternative reference reproduce −10.9 or −18.22 as an eclipse effect? No. Two multi-day quiet-day sets × four alignments give eclipse-window minima of −1.0 to −6.0 nT, all at 16:27 (four minutes after first contact, before meaningful obscuration). Only single-day references that leave the diurnal curve in (20 August, the dome's choice) give large values, and those minima fall at 19:14, the end of the window. Local time vs UT: Meza's '11:46 LT' is MDT (UT−6); solar time is UT−7h01m; rev2's 'near Boulder's local noon' is acceptable. USGS vs INTERMAGNET: data are INTERMAGNET definitive, as stated in _meta (script docstring wrong; hole 5). Where rev2 overreaches is precision, not direction: holes 0 and 1.
hnote_responses.ii_meza_citation: VERIFIED. Crossref: Amalia Meza, Guillermo Bosch, María Paula Natali, Bernardo Eylenstein, 'Ionospheric and geomagnetic response to the total solar eclipse on 21 August 2017', Advances in Space Research 69(1):16–25 (2022), doi 10.1016/j.asr.2021.07.029. Preprint arXiv:2107.12327v1 §3.2: at BOU 'the ∆X component shows positive values with its maximum arising near t0 ... the ∆Z component has the lower amplitude, showing positive values with its maximum near t0'; VIC/NEW (north of the path) show ∆Z negative after t0. Figure 7 read independently this run: BOU ∆X ≈ +10 nT, ∆Z ≈ +3.5 nT; model ∆X ≈ +8.5, ∆Z ≈ +3. The analyst's paraphrase is accurate. Method detail is incomplete in prose (hole 4).
hnote_responses.iii_verdict: KEEP 'Std Model Explains'. Rule (apply identically to our own claims): (1) 'Refuted by Data' requires the claimed observation to be contradicted at a stated reference by a test with power against the claimed amplitude. (2) A claimed signal that control days reproduce on the claimant's own statistic is not evidence for the claimed mechanism, but a non-discriminating number is not thereby refuted; it is reported as non-diagnostic. (3) Where the number is real and ordinary physics accounts for it, the verdict is 'Std Model Explains'. Applied here: the −18.22 nT is real (we reproduce it) and is explained by the ordinary Sq diurnal minimum (median of the other August days −19.9 nT on the same statistic); the −10.9 nT at 17:20 has no stated baseline and Boulder Z alone has ~±8 nT noise, so we have no powered test that refutes it. The dome itself has withdrawn the 2017 eclipse attribution (PROS-003), and the live WIN-010 (2016) is Sq timing coherence, also standard. 'Refuted by Data' would therefore be too harsh on what we can actually test, and 'Not Demonstrated' would understate that standard physics positively explains both the number and the real (X-dominated) eclipse effect. Symmetry check: this is the same rule Erratum 1 applied to our B1-M-001 band (met on 17 of 30 control days → 'little power to discriminate', not 'confirmed' and not 'refuted'). The text should say plainly that the 2017 number is not evidence of an eclipse effect; that is a statement about evidence, not a verdict change.

stronger_arguments.description: The dome's OPEN-009 'quiet-day baseline' (20 August 2017) was a Kp 5o / G1 storm day, more disturbed than the eclipse day it rejected as 'geomagnetically disturbed pre-eclipse' (peak 3o). This is internal to the dome and needs none of our physics (hole 2).

On the dome's own statistic, the eclipse day (−18.22 nT) sits near the median of the other 29 days of August 2017 (−19.9 nT; 16 of 29 at or below −18.22). The eclipse day is statistically ordinary on the measure the dome chose (hole 1).

Meza et al. find the dZ sign depends on station position relative to the path (BOU south: positive; VIC/NEW north: negative after t0). A one-signed 'Z dip' expectation is itself a misstatement of standard physics; this is already passed to EXP-687 rev4 via side_findings.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome is right that Boulder's Z reaches a low inside the 2017 eclipse window: −18.22 nT on its statistic, reproduced exactly here from the same 23 INTERMAGNET definitive files (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/win010-c17-rev2-verification-20260929.json:scripts[0].output.dome_open009_replication). It is right that 21 August 2017 was disturbed in the morning (GFZ Kp 3o at 06–09 UT). And there is a real eclipse effect at Boulder: Meza et al. 2022 measure ∆X ≈ +10 nT and ∆Z ≈ +3 nT near maximum (doi 10.1016/j.asr.2021.07.029, Figure 7).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The low the dome measures is Boulder's ordinary daily Z minimum near local solar noon: on the dome's own statistic the other 29 August 2017 days have a median of −19.9 nT (this review, hole 1). Its minimum falls at 19:07 UT, 81 minutes after eclipse maximum (EXP-684-rev2.json:field_patches.detail_evidence.new). The real eclipse effect at Boulder has the opposite sign in Z (Meza et al. 2022 §3.2). And the dome's 'quiet' reference day reached Kp 5o (05-model.txt:474 vs GFZ).

deeper_analysis: Attack from the dome side first: is our reference picked to erase the dome's number? No. Every multi-day quiet reference I tried (two sets, four alignments) puts eclipse-day Z within a few nT of quiet days at both 17:20 and maximum, and the only references that produce dome-sized dips are single days that leave the diurnal curve in, with the dip at the end of the window rather than at maximum. Then attack our side: the point values are below the noise of the method (LOO sd about 8 nT at one minute), and the five-quiet-day 'same measure' range is computed with a different statistic from the dome's. Both are fixable in sentences, and the corrected version is stronger: on the dome's exact statistic the eclipse day is at the median of August. The new material that hurts the dome most (20 August = Kp 5o) was in the analyst's own Kp input file and went unused. Meza et al. verified at bibliographic, text and figure level. Verdict logic: 'Std Model Explains' is the correct label under a rule we can apply to ourselves (see hnote_responses.iii). Separately, process note: git commit 320084e (2026-10-04 06:22Z), which carries the EXP-687-rev4 analyst outputs and the curmudgeon human-notes, has a KEV-analysis refresh commit message ('refresh 2026-10-02: KEV 1730->1731 ...'). Content is dome-correct, message is from another project. Audit-trail hygiene for the operator; nothing for the decider to patch.
